description: SPENVIS, the SPace ENVironment Information System, is a web-based system that gives spacecraft engineers and scientists access to models of the space environment and its effects. Models cover galactic cosmic rays, solar energetic particles, natural radiation belts, plasmas, gases, meteoroids and debris, and users combine them along a spacecraft trajectory to estimate environment and effects for mission design. It is developed by a consortium led by BIRA-IASB and maintained for ESA's Space Environments and Effects Section; version 4.6.14 was released on 5 March 2026. Coverage is Earth orbits and interplanetary space. Use is free of charge after registration, and the system is accessible online through a browser with JavaScript, with contextual help, a user forum and a bug tracker; some 3D outputs need a VRML or X3D plug-in. Caveats: it is a hosted service bound by its own terms and conditions, not open-source software, and results depend on the underlying empirical models. It supports space weather hazard exposure studies of satellites and space infrastructure; related records are NASA CCMC, the ESA Space Weather Service Network and SWMF.
